A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FTCT study and retain Sections 1-7 and Appendices A-M. Their text, equations, tables and matched figure content support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original FTCT experiments, including Transformer/MLP comparisons in Table 1, probing results in Table 3, and robustness and supplementary experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experimental results, including model comparisons, attention/probing analyses, and appendix evaluations with noise and incomplete reasoning paths.

M1.justification: The FTCT generation procedure, training objectives, underlying program in Algorithm 1, and Transformer construction remain unchanged. The revised related-work prose does not modify the method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate FTCT with clean and noisy test sequences, varying reasoning lengths, and missing intermediate steps. The newly referenced InfiBench is cited in the Introduction, not evaluated as an additional dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same five Transformer configurations and two- and four-layer MLPs. No evaluated comparator is added, removed or replaced.

E3.justification: Both retain the same graph-depth and child-chain settings, shot counts, accuracy metrics, and selection of optimal-shot performance in Table 1. The noisy-input, varying-length and incomplete-step evaluation procedures also match.

E4.justification: The architecture comparisons, noise robustness tests, knowledge-coverage check, shot/length analysis, attention/probing analyses and incomplete-step tests are retained. Appendices H-M contain the same analytical questions and evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix H.1 in both versions reports varying the causal structure five times per graph-depth/child-length pair and calculating averages and standard deviations. The uncertainty displays and reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 3 and 4 retain their numerical entries, and Figures 2-13 retain the same plotted results. For example, Table 1 whole-chain accuracy remains 1.000 for 2L2H and 0.002 for the four-layer MLP under the same settings.

T1.justification: Lemmas 5.1-5.3, Theorem 5.4, and the constructions and proofs in Appendices D-F are unchanged. The loss equations are renumbered without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims that few-shot CoT enables FTCT compositional reasoning, success depends on data similarity and model complexity, and Transformers can implement an underlying generalizable program.

C2.justification: Both retain the induction-head and parent-retrieval explanations, the distribution-mismatch explanation for extra-shot degradation in Appendix K, and the training-bias interpretation of incomplete-step failures in Appendix M. The limitation concerning transfer from synthetic tasks to real-world models also remains.

D1.justification: Appendices B and G retain the same generation and implementation details, including 720-dimensional embeddings, a 2048-token context window, AdamW at 5e-5, MLP window settings and probing dimensions. The printed code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v6 adds InfiBench (Li et al., 2024a), Physics of Language Models Part 3.2 (Allen-Zhu and Li, 2023a), and Jin et al. (2025). Section 2 adds a brief connection to architectural features supporting generalization, while the broader positioning of FTCT remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v6 lightly edits the abstract and introduction, rewrites the Transformer-expressivity paragraph, and corrects small errors such as 'Trainin' in Table 1 and 'differenxces' in Appendix K. Most prose and the section/appendix sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The entire paper adopts ICLR typesetting, changing typography, spacing, table dimensions, figure sizes and float placement. Figures 6-7 and 8-9 now share pages. The right-hand heatmaps in Figures 11-12 fit within the page, and Figure 13's caption no longer overlaps the page number. The underlying graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The clearest gains are presentational: v6 fixes the clipped right-hand heatmaps in Figures 11-12 and the caption/page-number overlap in Figure 13. Small prose corrections and additional research context provide limited further benefit. The denser layout uses smaller text and figures, while the scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is modest.
